title: Everyone called (Lumen Gentium 40)
hookLine: all are called to the fullness of Christian life
tomorrow: can Mary be a mother to us without taking from Christ?

cards: Search the word saint and the images are halos, robes and folded hands: people who never seem to wait in a parking lot or fold laundry. So here's an odd detail.

When Vatican II's document on the Church gets to holiness, it doesn't start with monks. It starts with Jesus asking for perfection from everybody: "Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect."
Everybody? Perfect? That sounds like a setup for failure, unless the council means something else by perfect.

teach.b: Paragraph forty solves it in four moves. First, who's asked. Jesus, it says, preached holiness of life to each and every one of his disciples, whatever their condition.
The chapter's title even uses the word universal: a universal call to holiness. Second, where holiness comes from.

teach.h: HOLY BY GRACE, NOT BY WORKS.
teach.b: Not from people's own works, the paragraph says, but from God's purpose and grace. In baptism they're made children of God and truly holy. So the job isn't to manufacture holiness.
It's to hold on to it and bring it to completion. Third, the honest part.
The same paragraph admits that we all stumble in many things, so we need God's mercy every day, and we pray, forgive us our trespasses. So perfect here can't mean flawless.

The call goes out to people who are still tripping. Fourth, the answer to the puzzle. All the faithful, of whatever rank or state, are called to the fullness of the Christian life and to the perfection of love.
Perfect, in this paragraph, is measured in love.
And the council adds a quiet line: holiness like this makes life on earth more human. The nurse on nights, the grandfather, the teenager, the bishop: one call, lived in different places.

how: Catholics speak of the universal call to holiness to mean that laypeople, in their work and family life, are called to holiness as fully as priests and religious, and parishes and lay movements build their teaching on it.

o: the call to holiness reaches all, in every way of life
a church bell rung to gather the whole town
a summons for each Catholic to become a priest

p: God's purpose and grace, not works

s: Vatican II taught that holiness is mainly for priests, monks and nuns
Lumen Gentium 40 calls all the faithful, of whatever rank or state.
Lumen Gentium 40 admits that everyone stumbles in many things
and so needs God's mercy every day.
the council says people make themselves holy by their own works
it says by God's purpose and grace; baptism makes them holy.

games.q: your coworker says she's given up on being "a good Catholic" because she keeps losing her temper in traffic. what does Lumen Gentium 40 offer her?
o: holiness is mostly for calmer people in religious life.
the call goes to people still stumbling; mercy is daily.
she has to stop losing her temper before she can begin.
games.why: the paragraph admits we all stumble in many things and need mercy every day. the call to the perfection of love doesn't wait for anyone to be finished.

practice: Choose one ordinary hour from tomorrow: a class, a shift, a ride home. Name one loving thing you'd like to happen in it, and then the thing most likely to get in the way.
Decide now what you'll do when that obstacle shows up, and rest with the plan while the timer runs.

wordCard.voice: Everyone called. Lumen Gentium's universal call: holiness, measured in love, for every baptized person.

orig.note: Latin for calling: chapter five of Lumen Gentium names a universal call to holiness.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: all called, the bishop and the teenager alike, including the ones still tripping. Until tomorrow.
